speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked	the Minister for Health for patients with mobility needs who are physically unable to visit the nearest polyclinic, what measures are available to arrange a subsidised medical assessment at home so that the patient can qualify for assistance from the Agency for Integrated Care, SG Enable and related agencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This can be done through AIC touchpoints, such as AICare Links at our acute hospitals, Singapore Silver Line and Singapore Silver Pages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We will continue to monitor the care needs in the community to ensure that our schemes and services are accessible to patients who require them.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regard to the second question about sharing of the results of the mobility and medical assessments, we note the requirement and the need to minimise such assessments as much as possible to reduce inconvenience, particularly for the frail elderly.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: However, as different schemes may have different eligibility criteria to ensure that we target the right group of beneficiaries, clients may, in some instances, still need to undergo additional assessments for schemes with different or additional criteria.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: However, we are mindful of this and we will try to minimise this as much as possible.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As Minister Tan Chuan-Jin had said, MOH and the Ministry of Social and Family Development work very closely together.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, AIC and SG Enable, if need to, we will also share information on the medical and mobility assessments.
